title: Quasi-coherent derived pushforward and its coproduct comparison
statement: Work in the fixed universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For an algebraic space $Z$ over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], use its small etale structure sheaf $\mathcal O_Z$, module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the full subcategory of objects whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$. Here quasi-compactness is tested after pullback to every affine scheme over $Y$, and quasi-separatedness means the relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Use the canonical module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], and let $Rf_*$ be its unbounded right derived functor computed on K-injective resolutions. Then $Rf_*$ sends $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ into $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. For every small family $(E_i)$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, the map $\bigoplus_i Rf_*E_i\to Rf_*(\bigoplus_iE_i)$ induced by the coproduct injections is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_Y)$. The coproducts are the ambient derived coproducts (computed by termwise direct sums of representatives). No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of the individual spaces is required unless explicitly stated.

source.place: Tag 08FA, lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-image, part (1); Tag 08FB, lemma-quasi-coherence-pushforward-direct-sums; ambient sums: Tag 08F3, lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-sums.

proof.text: Use the small site skeletons fixed by the size convention. The module categories on the small etale sites are Grothendieck abelian. Their ambient derived coproducts are represented by termwise sums. Exactness of sums implies $H^q(\bigoplus_iE_i)=\bigoplus_iH^q(E_i)$ and that good truncations commute with these sums: compute their kernels and cokernels termwise. Quasi-coherent modules are closed under sums, kernels and cokernels. Consequently the ambient sum of the $E_i$ has quasi-coherent cohomology, as do their good truncations.

Restrict to affine etale scheme charts $a:V\to Y$, putting $X_V=X\times_YV$ and $g:X_V\to V$. The chart calculus identifies $a^*Rf_*K$ with $Rg_*(K|_{X_V})$, and quasi-coherent cohomology is detected on these charts. Restriction to a slice commutes with sums: the sheafified termwise sum restricts to the sheafified sum on that slice, since its coverings are exactly the coverings over the slice object. It is exact, so it also commutes with good truncations and cohomology. These identifications take each coprojection to its restricted coprojection, hence identify the restricted canonical comparison with the comparison for $g$. The hypotheses on $g$ follow directly from the scheme-test definitions: every affine test over $V$ is one over $Y$, and the diagonal is a base change of the diagonal of $f$. We may thus prove both claims with $Y$ affine. Isomorphisms of sheaves are detected on a covering by the sheaf gluing axiom.

source.place: Tag 08FA, proof: first localization on Y; Tag 08FB, local interpretation of the choice of N

proof.text: The canonical module direct image is left exact: its adjunction identifies maps into the image of a kernel with maps into that kernel, so it preserves kernels and the zero object; it is additive by its module-valued limit formula. For bounded below $K$ with quasi-coherent cohomology, apply the truncation spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*H^q(K)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(Rf_*K)$. Its $E_2$ terms are quasi-coherent by the higher-image theorem. Every next page is a kernel modulo an image of maps between such modules, so remains quasi-coherent. In each fixed total degree, the spectral sequence stabilizes and the abutment has a finite filtration. Each graded piece is therefore quasi-coherent; induction through that finite filtration, starting at zero and using extension closure, proves that every $H^r(Rf_*K)$ is quasi-coherent.

On this affine target choose one $N\geq1$ from the uniform upper-bound lemma. Fix $r\in\mathbf Z$ and put $l=r-N$. For $A=\tau_{\leq l-1}K$ the bound gives $H^m(Rf_*A)=0$ for $m\geq l-1+N=r-1$, in particular for $m=r,r+1$. Apply $Rf_*$ to the truncation triangle $A\to K\to\tau_{\geq l}K\to A[1]$. Its long exact cohomology sequence gives the natural isomorphism $H^r(Rf_*K)\cong H^r(Rf_*\tau_{\geq l}K)$. The right side is quasi-coherent by the bounded below case. This proves preservation for arbitrary $K$; the chart reduction then proves it on the original target.

For every $p\geq0$, $R^pf_*$ preserves arbitrary sums of module sheaves. Indeed, the sum is the filtered colimit of its finite subsums, indexed by finite subsets of the indexing set (including the empty subset). The filtered-colimit lemma identifies its higher image with the colimit of the higher images of those finite subsums. Additivity of $R^pf_*$ identifies the latter with the finite subsums of $\bigoplus_iR^pf_*M_i$: applying the additive derived functor and then cohomology preserves finite biproducts. All identifications agree with the injections, so the resulting isomorphism is the canonical comparison.

For a family $K_i$ of objects with quasi-coherent cohomology and a common lower cohomological bound $a$, put $K=\bigoplus_iK_i$ with its coprojections $u_i:K_i\to K$; by step 1, $H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$. The module categories are Grothendieck abelian and $f_*$ is left exact and additive (step 3). By part 2 of the truncation spectral-sequence theorem applied to $M[0]$, $H^p(Rf_*(M[0]))\cong R^pf_*M$ naturally in the module $M$. Fix $p\geq0$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$. Under these identifications the canonical map $\bigoplus_iH^p(Rf_*(H^r(K_i)[0]))\to H^p(Rf_*(H^r(K)[0]))$ induced by the $H^r(u_i)$ is the composite of $\bigoplus_iR^pf_*H^r(K_i)\to R^pf_*(\bigoplus_iH^r(K_i))$, an isomorphism by step 5, with $R^pf_*$ of the canonical map $\bigoplus_iH^r(K_i)\to H^r(K)$, an isomorphism because $H^r$ preserves coproducts. So every hypothesis of the bounded-below coproduct filtration lemma holds for $F=f_*$, the maps $u_i$ and the bound $a$. For each degree $q$ it gives finite filtrations of $\bigoplus_iH^q(Rf_*K_i)$ and $H^q(Rf_*K)$ and a filtered morphism between them whose underlying map is the canonical comparison $\sum_iH^q(Rf_*u_i)$, with every graded map an isomorphism. The finite-filtration induction lemma shows that this comparison is an isomorphism, in every degree $q$, including $q<a$ and the empty family.

source.place: Tag 08FB, spectral-sequence reduction to a direct sum of quasi-coherent sheaves; natural comparison through the existing bounded-below coproduct filtration

proof.text: For the original unbounded family and a fixed degree $r$, take the single cutoff $l=r-N$ from step 4, with $N$ independent of the family. That step gives natural degree-$r$ isomorphisms for every $E_i$ and for $E=\bigoplus_iE_i$. Since $\tau_{\geq l}E=\bigoplus_i\tau_{\geq l}E_i$, step 6 gives the degree-$r$ comparison for the truncated family. Naturality with respect to each injection makes the square of truncated and untruncated degree-$r$ comparisons commute. Its two vertical arrows and bottom arrow are isomorphisms; hence so is its top arrow. By cohomology of ambient sums this top arrow is $H^r$ of the requested comparison. This holds for every $r$. A derived morphism inducing isomorphisms in all degrees is invertible: represent it by a roof with left arrow a quasi-isomorphism; the right arrow is then a quasi-isomorphism too, and both arrows are inverted by localization. This also covers the empty family. Finally restrict to the affine charts of step 2 to conclude globally.

proof_origin.place: Tags 08F3, 08FA and 08FB; explicit localization and natural spectral-sequence comparison
